Schema (the tables most likely to be needed):
code_lookup - Meaning of every coded column in the other tables: code_type (which code list: ORD_STATUS, TIER, REFUND_STATUS, REFUND_REASON, TKT_CATEG, REGION, CHANNEL, DEPT); code_val (the stored code); code_desc (what the code means in words)
cust_master - Customer master record: cust_id (customer id, like C-1002); cust_nm (customer name); tier_cd (loyalty tier: P platinum, G gold, S standard); region_cd (sales region: NA, EU, AP, LA); signup_dt (date the customer signed up); is_actv (1 = active, 0 = closed or inactive (soft delete)); email_addr (contact email address); phone_no (contact phone number)
ord_hdr - Order header, one row per order: ord_id (order id, like O-5002); cust_id (customer who placed the order); ord_dt (order date); ord_status (N new, S shipped, D delivered, C cancelled, R returned); ord_total_amt (order total in the ORDER currency (currency_cd), already net of line discounts); currency_cd (currency of ord_total_amt); channel_cd (sales channel: WEB, APP, PHN, STR)  FK: cust_id->cust_master.cust_id
support_tkt - Support tickets: tkt_id (ticket id, like T-70010); cust_id (customer who raised the ticket); opened_ts (when the ticket was opened); closed_ts (when it was closed; NULL means the ticket is still open); sev_lvl (severity: 1 critical, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low); categ_cd (category: BILL billing, SHIP shipping, TECH technical, ACCT account, REFD refunds); assigned_emp_id (employee working it; NULL if not yet assigned); channel_cd (how it arrived: WEB, APP, PHN, STR)  FK: cust_id->cust_master.cust_id
inv_move - Stock movements: mv_id (movement id); sku (product moved); wh_id (warehouse it moved in or out of); mv_ts (when it moved); mv_type (IN restock, OUT customer shipment, ADJ stock count correction); qty (units moved: positive for IN, negative for OUT, either sign for ADJ); ord_id (order that caused an OUT movement; NULL for IN and ADJ)
shipment - Shipments, one per shipped order: ship_id (shipment id, like S-8001); ord_id (order shipped); wh_id (warehouse it left from); carrier_cd (carrier: UPS, DHL, FDX, USP); ship_dt (date handed to the carrier); deliv_dt (date delivered; NULL until delivered); ship_status (shipment state: I in transit, D delivered)  FK: ord_id->ord_hdr.ord_id
cust_segment_hist - Monthly history of each customer segment: cust_id (customer); month_dt (first day of the month the segment applied); segment_cd (segment that month: NEW, REG regular, VIP, RISK at risk of leaving)  FK: cust_id->cust_master.cust_id
Find all shipments handled by either 'UPS' or 'FDX' that were shipped in the month of January 2026. Return the shipment ID, order ID, carrier code, and ship date.

```sql
SELECT ship_id, ord_id, carrier_cd, ship_dt FROM shipment WHERE carrier_cd IN ('UPS', 'FDX') AND ship_dt BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-01-31' ORDER BY ship_dt, ship_id
```

```

WITH promo_rev AS (SELECT T1.promo_cd, T1.promo_nm, SUM(T3.ord_total_amt) AS rev FROM promo AS T1 INNER JOIN ord_promo AS T2 ON T1.promo_id = T2.promo_id INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS T3 ON T2.ord_id = T3.ord_id WHERE T3.ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND T3.ord_dt <= '2026-12-31' GROUP BY T1.promo_cd, T1.promo_nm), total_rev AS (SELECT SUM(rev) AS grand_rev FROM promo_rev) SELECT T.promo_cd, T.promo_nm, T.rev, (T.rev * 100.0 / TR.grand_rev) AS pct_of_total FROM promo_rev AS T CROSS JOIN total_rev AS TR ORDER BY pct_of_total DESC
```

List the customer id and customer name for these at-risk customers, ordered alphabetically by customer name, then by customer id.

```sql
SELECT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN web_event AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t2.channel_cd = 'WEB' AND t2.evt_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND t2.evt_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' AND t1.cust_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-04-01') GROUP BY t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm ORDER BY t1.cust_nm ASC, t1.cust_id ASC
```

A late shipment is defined as a shipment where the delivery date is later than the ship date plus 5 days. Show the warehouse ID, the count of late shipments, and the average days between ship date and delivery date for each warehouse, considering only shipments dispatched in '2026-01', ordered by the count of late shipments descending then warehouse ID ascending.

```sql
SELECT wh_id, COUNT(*) AS late_count, AVG(DATEDIFF(deliv_dt, ship_dt)) AS avg_transit_days FROM shipment WHERE ship_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ship_dt <= '2026-01-31' AND deliv_dt > DATE_ADD(ship_dt, INTERVAL 5 DAY) GROUP BY wh_id ORDER BY late_count DESC, wh_id ASC
```

A high-revenue product category is defined as a category where the total gross revenue (quantity multiplied by unit price) exceeds 200.00. Show the category code, the count of unique SKUs sold in that category, and the total revenue, ordered by total revenue descending, then category code ascending.

```sql
SELECT p.categ_cd, COUNT(DISTINCT p.sku) AS sku_cnt, SUM(l.qty * l.unit_prc) AS total_rev FROM prod_catalog p JOIN ord_line l ON p.sku = l.sku GROUP BY p.categ_cd HAVING SUM(l.qty * l.unit_prc) > 200.00 ORDER BY total_rev DESC, categ_cd ASC
```

```sql
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(t2.ord_dt, '%Y-%m') AS mth, t3.categ_cd, SUM(t1.qty * t1.unit_prc * (1 - t1.disc_pct / 100.0)) AS monthly_revenue FROM ord_line AS t1 INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id INNER JOIN prod_catalog AS t3 ON t1.sku = t3.sku WHERE t2.ord_dt >= '2025-10-01' AND t2.ord_dt <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(t2.ord_dt, '%Y-%m'), t3.categ_cd ORDER BY mth ASC, t3.categ_cd ASC
```

```sql

```
